_comment: The claim registry additions of 14-ghost-design §10.3 (11-brand §8 holds C1 to C23). tools/check-copy.py check (4): a copy sentence that carries one of a claim's markers must be one of its registered sentences ({variables} match their value, or nothing where a page binds it with data-v); a claim with `requires` needs that sentence on the same page, or a link to where it is stated (`requires_link`). `labels` are buttons and headings that carry a marker without making a claim.

claims.condition: always (child form of C1)
sentences: It gets locked right here, before it goes anywhere.

claims.condition: link modes (child form of C2)
sentences: The key hides in the link, after the # sign.

claims.condition: always (child form of C1; the server also sees the C3 and C4 metadata, said on /made#who)
sentences: Our server gets scrambled noise. Never the key.

claims.condition: always; downloads in progress delay it up to {ticket_min} minutes; C5-snap and C6 apply
sentences: We delete our scrambled copy.
Then it's gone. We delete our scrambled copy.

claims.condition: after the exit is in a SealLog checkpoint; before it, the pending form
sentences: Its goodbye is written on the Tari chain, for anyone to check.
We wrote its goodbye on the Tari chain.
Its goodbye goes on the Tari chain within {checkpoint_min} minutes.

claims.condition: every exit is added to SealLog at the next checkpoint (within {checkpoint_min} minutes); it proves we said we deleted it, not that we kept no copy
sentences: Then it's gone, and its goodbye goes on the Tari chain.

claims.condition: /verify checks the inclusion proof against the SealLog root on chain; the judges' demo secret is burned at least {checkpoint_min} minutes before the tag
sentences: Its goodbye on the Tari chain, checked by your browser.

claims.condition: courier sends; relay mode means we learn the address (C8)
sentences: Or send it to a Tari address. Only they can open it.
It goes by Tari. Only they can open it.
Send by Tari: the key rides inside a payment to their address. Only they can open it.

claims.condition: rule Once (the default); gone = the link ends and C24 applies; an unopened link ends at its expiry
sentences: You get a link. Your friend sees it once.
It opens one time in the next {anon_max_expiry}. Then it's gone.
Same link. Now it opens one time.
It opens one time. When you open it, it's gone.
It opens one time, until {date}. Then the link ends.
It opens one time. Then the link ends.

claims.condition: rule A few times: min(3, max_views), set in place only while views_used = 0
sentences: It opens up to {few} times in the next {anon_max_expiry}. Then it's gone.
Same link. Now it opens up to {few} times.
It opens up to {few} times, until {date}. Then the link ends.
It opens up to {few} times. Then the link ends.

claims.condition: kind 3 only (the default send and every dead drop); kind 4 files open with that wallet's view key, so C15 sits on every view-key screen; deleted if only kind 4 ships (spec G2)
markers: no file sent to your locker
lists arrivals and opens no file
claims.requires: A view key can't spend, but it can read everything sent to this address, including files.
sentences: For files sent to your locker: you see that something came, and how much. Not the file.
What came, and how much. No file sent to your locker opens with it.
For files sent to a locker, the view-key screen lists arrivals and opens no file. Files sent to another wallet open with its view key.

claims.condition: lockers
sentences: We store a random id and a hash of your login key. No email and no public key; a dead drop stores its own address, by design.

claims.condition: adding or removing a secret word
claims.backed_by: spec §5.4 (a password is a new link and the old one is revoked)
sentences: This makes a new link. The old one stops working.
New link made. The old one stopped working.

claims.condition: every money screen (child form of C19)
sentences: {network} testnet: tTARI is test money, worth nothing. Ootle mainnet: {mainnet_date}.
{network} testnet: tTARI is test money, worth nothing. The Ootle mainnet is live; {brand} stays on the testnet until our code is reviewed.

claims.condition: locker onboarding (child form of C17)
markers: lives in this browser. No email
nobody can let you back in
sentences: It lives in this browser. No email, no password.
Save your key. If this browser forgets it, nobody can let you back in, not even us.

claims.condition: QR caption under rule Once
claims.backed_by: spec §5.3 (the reveal gate burns only on Open it)
sentences: Scan it to open it on a phone. That uses its one look.
Scan it to open it on a phone. That uses its one open.

claims.condition: always
sentences: Files lock in this browser before upload.
They lock in this browser before they upload.

claims.condition: pay to open (features.pay_to_open)
sentences: You pay the owner's Tari address directly. We never hold the money.
The money goes straight to your Tari address. We never hold it.
Our demo wallet pays the owner for you, with test money.

claims.condition: pay to open, on /made#pay with its limits (C34, C38, R4) on the same page
sentences: The money goes straight to the owner's Tari address; our server keeps half of the key and hands it to the buyer once Tari's chain shows the payment, so the owner can be offline and we never hold the money or the whole key.

claims.condition: paid links; sB lives in backups for {db_backup_days} days
sentences: We keep half of the key and give it to you once the chain shows your payment. The other half is in the link, which we never see. Neither half opens it alone.
If the link leaks, our server could open it too.
We keep half of the key and give it to each buyer once the chain shows their payment. The other half is in the link. Neither half opens it alone.

claims.condition: sellers, shown the first time they sell
sentences: To see who paid you, we keep your sales view key. It is sealed, so a copy of our database can't read it. Our payment checker on our server can. A view key can see payments, never spend them.
For pay links: each payment's amount and hour, read with your sealed sales view key

claims.condition: every way to pay
markers: hidden amount and a hidden owner
hides the amount and who got it
sentences: The chain shows a payment with a hidden amount and a hidden owner. The fee is public.
Test money comes from our demo wallet, so it can be grouped with our other payments.
Pay to open: they pay your Tari address, then it opens. The chain hides the amount and who got it. The fee is public.

claims.condition: pay page, before Pay
sentences: Payments can't be taken back, by us or by Tari. Pay only if what you see here is enough.

claims.condition: non-test payments, only if the gated release ships
sentences: Paid from your own wallet? It opens after the owner's drive checks it.
We check the amount and that the payment is on the chain. Only the owner's drive can check the money is theirs to spend.
Paid. The owner's drive checks it next time it opens.
The owner's drive checks it

claims.condition: pay page
sentences: Paying lets you open it {buyer_views} times until {date}. Anyone who opens a file can pass it on. The owner can still delete it.

claims.condition: always (activity)
markers: who opened it or their ip
sentences: We count opens per hour. We never store who opened it or their IP address.

claims.condition: folders
sentences: Our server sees which files share a folder, how deep it goes and how many files are in it. Never a name.
Which folder it is in, and how many files sit beside it

claims.condition: only for files that leave; never for a link ending on a kept file
markers: write that on the tari chain
wrote that on the tari chain
goes on the tari chain within
sentences: When a file leaves your drive, we write that on the Tari chain, for anyone to check.
It left your drive. We wrote that on the Tari chain.
That goes on the Tari chain within {checkpoint_min} minutes.
After that, it leaves your drive. We write that on the Tari chain.
The file left our server. We wrote that on the Tari chain.
We write that on the Tari chain.
We wrote that on the Tari chain.
That goes on the Tari chain within {checkpoint}.

claims.condition: always
sentences: Search runs in this browser. Our server can't read your file names.

claims.condition: always (child of C3 with C40, C41)
markers: so the real size stays hidden
sentences: A padded size, so the real size stays hidden
What it never stores: the name, the type, what's inside, the key, who opened it, or their IP address.
What it never stores

claims.condition: always (open = sign in, last_seen_day)
sentences: If you don't open your drive for {inactive_days} days, we delete what's in it.

claims.condition: packs; trash first after step 4
sentences: When extra space ends, nothing goes for {lapse_grace_days} days. Then files in the trash go first, then the oldest, until you fit.

claims.condition: trash (server state, annex §2.4)
sentences: Files in the trash still use space. We empty it after {trash_days} days. Links add no space.
Its links stop working now. You can bring it back for {trash_days} days.

public_key: A sentence about what we store may name public keys only to say we store none (C29).
